sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Prabandha Style**: A dominant literary genre in Telugu literature characterized by complex narrative structures, elaborate descriptions (varnanas), and the use of 'Ashtadiggajas' (eight poets) in the court of Krishnadevaraya.
• **Multilingualism**: The empire functioned as a bridge between Sanskrit scholarship and regional vernaculars, fostering a 'Sanskrit-Vernacular' synthesis.
• **Patronage Mechanism**: Royal courts served as 'literary hubs' where poets were granted 'Agraharas' (land grants) to sustain intellectual production.
• **Key Metric**: The transition from religious-centric texts to secular/courtly poetry (Kavya) marks the evolution of Vijayanagar literary output.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Literary Synthesis**: Integration of Sanskrit Puranic themes into regional Telugu/Kannada narratives.
• **Institutional Support**: The role of the Sringeri and Hampi Virupaksha temples as centers for manuscript preservation.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Loss of palm-leaf manuscripts due to climatic conditions and post-1565 (Battle of Talikota) destruction.
• **Solutions**: Digital archiving of epigraphic records and critical editions of classical texts.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-A-K' (Prabandha, Ashtadiggajas, Krishnadevaraya).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Prabandha style) was the peak of A (Ashtadiggajas) under K (Krishnadevaraya).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Amuktamalyada' as being written by a court poet. Remember: It is attributed to Krishnadevaraya himself.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Literary Cosmopolitanism' to describe how Vijayanagar integrated diverse linguistic traditions into a unified imperial identity.

keyTakeaways: Krishnadevaraya's reign is the zenith of Telugu literature (Prabandha style).
The Haridasa movement represents the democratization of Kannada literature.
Vijayanagar literature was not just religious; it was a sophisticated blend of courtly, philosophical, and devotional traditions.
